detailed_rows.source_state: Comment p.638 (printed 621) prints the construction: 'Let mu_omega2 and nu_omega2 be the conditional distributions of omega1 and omega3 given omega2. Then let (omega1, omega2, omega3) have the law where (omega1, omega3) has conditional law mu_omega2 x nu_omega2 given omega2.' It adds an external pointer (Billingsley 1995, Exercise 18.20) for constructing a law from specified conditional distributions, and a finite-A route through Kolmogorov's existence theorem.

counted_H2_note: Two keys, 7.7 and 7.10, are recorded as countable complete H2 material because the printed Comment covers the full stated target and every residue is an immediate support check, a pointwise restatement, or a degenerate case. dissenting_or_open_points.point: The Comment prints the construction but not the one-step check that each witness conditional kernel is supported inside the ordering set, and it defers the existence of the conditional distributions to Billingsley (1995), Exercise 18.20. If that check is held to be substantive rather than immediate, this row falls to H2_material_incomplete_full_target. I read it as immediate, because the support comes from the defining witness couplings.

Part (a) is proved in the Comment in five sentences. Part (b) receives nothing. The row is kept in the H2 family so that the printed (a) is not lost, and is marked H2_core_complete false so that it cannot be counted as a core for the full target. A reviewer who reads the H2-family label as a count would be wrong; the label alone is not the count.

The periodic case is handled in one sentence and the pointwise bound is not restated there; the degenerate case of a vertex with no return is not mentioned at all. None of these is a gap in the non-routine core, but a stricter pass could ask for them explicitly.

The body prints (7.2) as a display and then asks for its proof. Anyone reading the display as printed material would overstate this row; the display is the target. Recorded so that the confusion is on the record rather than latent.

The exercise asks to extend Theorem 7.20 to quasi-transitive graphs. I record the printed proof as material of Theorem 7.20 and the adaptation as the burden. A pass that counted the printed proof as 7.8's material would double-count a theorem already counted in the body.

The author's Harris hint for 7.2 is printed under 7.20, outside this block. If a later pass were to treat sibling Comments as material for the key they mention, 7.2 would move to H1_residual_recommendation. This report does not do that, and the locator is recorded instead.
